checks.name: SPF
checks.summary: 1 record, 1/10 DNS lookups, 0/2 void lookups, ends with ~all

findings.title: SPF ends with ~all (softfail)
findings.explanation: '~all' vs '-all' is a policy choice. With DMARC enforcing, '~all' is common and safe; '-all' asks receivers to reject unlisted senders outright, which can also break forwarded mail.

checks.name: DMARC
details: DKIM alignment adkim=r (relaxed: subdomains of the same organisational domain align)
SPF alignment aspf=r (relaxed: subdomains of the same organisational domain align)

findings.title: DMARC policy is p=none (monitoring only)
findings.explanation: p=none tells receivers to take no action on mail that fails DMARC: spoofed mail is still delivered normally. It is the right first stage while you read the aggregate reports, but it does not protect the domain. Staged path: (1) p=none with rua reports while you check that every legitimate sender passes SPF or DKIM with alignment; (2) p=quarantine (optionally with pct below 100 at first) so failing mail goes to spam; (3) p=reject once reports stay clean.

findings.title: No MTA-STS record
findings.explanation: MTA-STS makes senders require TLS with a valid certificate when delivering to your MX hosts, blocking downgrade attacks. To enable it, serve a policy file as text/plain at https://mta-sts.demarkstudio.ca/.well-known/mta-sts.txt (valid HTTPS certificate for mta-sts.demarkstudio.ca) with mode: testing first, then publish the TXT record. Policy file: (one line each) version: STSv1 | mode: testing | mx: smtp.google.com | max_age: 604800

findings.title: No TLS-RPT record
findings.explanation: TLS-RPT asks senders to email you daily reports of TLS problems delivering to your domain; useful alongside MTA-STS.

checks.name: BIMI
details: BIMI shows your logo in some inboxes; it needs DMARC p=quarantine or p=reject and, for Gmail, a verified mark certificate.
